cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: The /admin/vendors* entry in src/api/middlewares.ts runs authenticate with allowUnauthenticated so the invite-acceptance endpoint can be reached from an email link, and neither handler here looks at req.auth_context: GET returns an atelier's remittance history and payout IBAN suffix for any req.params.id, and POST opens a payout batch, so both are reachable with no session at all.

cases.why: Both handlers sit under the same permissive /admin/vendors* matcher but call requireStaffActor first, which returns null unless req.auth_context.actor_type is "user", and the route answers 401 on null; the update then copies only the four named profile fields and rejects a feed_url that is not absolute https.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: GET resolves the registry from req.params.id alone and returns the owner's shipping address, recipient email, private note, store credit and every guest's claim email, so any authenticated customer can read any other customer's registry by id; the DELETE handler in the same file shows the customer_id filter that GET is missing, and registry.visibility is never consulted either.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: loadOwnedRegistry resolves the registry with { id, customer_id: req.auth_context.actor_id } - plus the publishable key's sales channels when the storefront scoped any - so a registry id belonging to another customer resolves to null and both handlers answer 404 before any claim is read or written.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: The handler is typed with the validated schema but hands em.assign the raw req.body, and validateAndTransformBody puts the parsed, stripped object on req.validatedBody rather than replacing req.body, so assign writes every GiftRegistry property the payload happens to name - customer_id, store_credit_cents, is_verified and sales_channel_id included - and persistAndFlush commits it.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: This handler reads req.validatedBody, the stripped object produced by validateAndTransformBody against a strict schema, and then hands em.assign an object built from three explicitly named fields, so a payload carrying customer_id, is_verified or store_credit_cents never reaches the entity.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: from, to, state, vendor_id, sort and direction are read off req.query and interpolated into the string passed to em.getConnection().execute() - inside single quotes in the WHERE clause and bare after ORDER BY - so a crafted state or sort value runs attacker-chosen SQL under the application's database role.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: The same raw grouped join through em.getConnection().execute(), but vendor_id, status, both date bounds and the limit ride in as bind parameters, the state is checked against BATCH_STATES, and the only interpolated fragment is an ORDER BY expression looked up in the SORT_COLUMNS allowlist with a two-valued direction.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: req.query.page is joined onto DOCUMENT_ROOT and the document's storage_folder with no basename, extension or prefix check, so ?page=../../../../etc/passwd resolves outside the document folder and createReadStream streams it back; the membership check above only decides which document id may be addressed, not which file.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: resolveAttachment does the work: it rejects extensions outside CONTENT_TYPES, strips any directory component with path.basename, requires the resolved path to equal the plain join of folder and name, and then requires realpath to still start with the attachment folder, so a ../ or a symlink in req.query.file yields null and a 404.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: vendor.feed_url is a value the atelier types into the vendor portal, and the step passes it straight to fetch() with no scheme or host check and default redirect following, so an atelier can aim the platform's sync at http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or any service inside the cluster; the admin route that stores feed_url only requires https, which does not constrain the host.

cases.architecture: Medusa 2 commerce backend in TypeScript: file-based API routes under src/api (store and admin prefixes, [id] segments), a custom marketplace module whose data layer is MikroORM 6 over Postgres accessed through an EntityManager, and the caller's identity taken from req.auth_context (actor_type "customer" or "user") set by the authenticate middleware declared in src/api/middlewares.ts.
cases.why: resolveAssetUrl parses the atelier-supplied base together with the requested path and returns a URL only when the scheme is https, the port is empty or 443, and the hostname is one of the four origins in ALLOWED_ASSET_HOSTS; the fetch also sets redirect: "error", so a vendor-controlled value cannot steer the request at an internal host.
